newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - No policy changes seen at coffee talks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - No policy changes seen at coffee talks.

text.p: The Association of Coffee Producing Countries technical group will review the market at a session in Costa Rica this weekend but no major policy revisions are likely, ACPC secretary-general Roberio Oliveira said on Wednesday.
He also said in an interview with Reuters that the outlook for prices was positive and supply tightness could be around for a while.
"I'm very optimistic about the state of the market," he said. "Every single day, we are seeing the tightness in the market".
"Considering the situation at the New York exchange, the tight market situation is going to stay for a while," he added.
US certified coffee stocks have fallen to around 800 60-kg bags, the lowest level since New York's Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange began tracking stock data in 1980.
Oliveria also reiterated that stocks continue at a level that does not give much comfort margin to the industry.
Information about industry purchases and roasting levels in the United States suggested that coffee that was being bought was being roasted immediately.
The November 9-10 meeting of the ACPC technical group will be held alongside the annual international Coffee Week, known as Sintercafe in Spanish, in Costa Rica.
Sintercafe runs from November 9 to 13
The technical group is made up of representatives of Brazil, Colombia, El Salvador, Indonesia, Ivory Coast and Uganda.
The full 14-member ACPC council accounts for more than 80 percent of world coffee production.
The ACPC agreed last May to limit green coffee exports from its members to 53.5 million 60-kg bags in the year to June 1997 against 45.8 million in the previous 12 months.
"It's obvious that we are going to keep an eye on the market but the evaluation (of the programme) is really going to be based on the first semester," Oliveria said.
"The main topic on the agenda of the meeting is to evaluate the market situation...how we see the behaviour of prices," he said.
Asked if the group planned some modifications to the export targets, Oliveria said: "No."
Any changes, if necessary, will only be considered at the next technical group meeting in February either in Colombia or Indonesia.
The ACPC said in September that exports for the year ended last June were 44.83 million bags, slightly below its target limit of 45.8 million.
Some producer sources said the Costa Rica meeting was held because of dissatisfaction on the part of Central American producers with internal share-outs of exports in the first half of 1997.
Brazil is not looking to increase six million bag share in the first half of 1997 and traders saw no problem Brazil keeping to nine million bag limit in July-December this year.
